prompt: Image 1 shows the official UI pieces of our pixel-art school game: a cream speech-bubble panel with a dark green (#294b40) stepped pixel outline, and dark green pixel glyphs "!" and "?". Image 2 shows how a small "!" speech bubble floats above a character on the map. Image 3 is a game background for colour mood. Draw a clean GAME UI SPRITE SHEET with exactly THREE separate small map marker icons in one row, evenly spaced, each centred in its own third of the image, on a perfectly flat plain pure WHITE background (#ffffff) with lots of empty white space around every icon. No shadows on the background, no ground, no scenery, no text, no letters except the glyphs. Icon A (destination marker, "go here"): a chunky map PIN shaped like an upside-down teardrop pointing straight DOWN, honey gold (#f3cf72) fill with a lighter top-left highlight, dark green (#294b40) 1-pixel stepped outline, and a bold cream (#fff9e7) exclamation mark "!" inside the round head. Icon B (talk marker, "something is up, come talk"): a small rounded square cream (#fff9e7) speech bubble with a short pointed tail at the bottom centre, dark green (#294b40) stepped pixel outline, and a bold dark green question mark "?" in the middle, exactly in the style of image 1. Icon C: the same speech bubble as B but with a pale honey (#fbe7a6) fill and a dark green "?". Style: crisp 16-bit pixel art on a coarse 16x16 pixel grid per icon, every pixel a big clearly visible square block, only 4 to 6 flat colours, no gradients, no anti-aliasing, no glow, no drop shadow, calm and friendly, not flashy.
